clue.text: Is flipping Tarzan right for the title role?

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over end to end, so the jungle hero's other name is read backwards

blocks.note: Tarzan is the ape-man of Edgar Rice Burroughs's stories
rt is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A casting director wonders whether an acrobatic Tarzan really suits the starring role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as Tarzan's somersaults or a mild British oath; it turns his nickname, the ape-man, back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A title role is the character a play or film is named after, so it is the part carrying the work's name.

clue.text: Crazy about rock

indicators.note: 'about' suggests turning round, so the word for crazy is read from its end back to its start

explanation.surface: Someone is mad about rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music genre, but it is a verb meaning to shake or shock someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock someone is to shock or daze them badly, which is what stunning a person does.

clue.text: Refuge for youth leader in a squalid district

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of youth is kept
'in' places one piece inside the phrase that follows it

blocks.note: a slum is a squalid run-down district

explanation.surface: A shelter for a youth worker set up in a deprived neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or sanctuary granted to someone in danger, a synonym of refuge.

clue.text: Dance about repeatedly on outskirts of Brazilian city

indicators.note: pieces placed on the outskirts of something sit on its edges, surrounding it

blocks.note: ca is the abbreviation for circa, about
repeatedly means the abbreviation for about appears a second time

explanation.surface: A dance performed again and again on the edge of a Brazilian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for about appears twice, one on each side of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The carioca is a Brazilian ballroom dance resembling the samba, named after natives of Rio.

clue.text: Crazy, like "The" in the Guardian's logo?

indicators.note: 'in' places the comparison phrase inside the word meaning crazy

explanation.surface: A quirky remark about how the Guardian prints the word 'The' in its title block.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian's printed title once read 'The Guardian'; the clue's own newspaper supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is the title banner printed across the top of a newspaper's front page, carrying its name.

clue.text: Circus performer - a heretic or revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns the existing order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A circus act described as a dissenting radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circus' suggests clowns and trapezes, but the Roman circus was a chariot-racing arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer raced chariots in the ancient Roman circus, the arena for such contests, so was a performer there.

clue.text: German and Swiss leader and French and Norwegian novelist

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Swiss is kept

explanation.surface: A list of nationalities building to a Norwegian writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sigrid Undset won the 1928 Nobel Prize in Literature for her medieval Norwegian novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigrid Undset was a Norwegian author of novels such as Kristin Lavransdatter, so she fits the description.

clue.text: An animated film enthusiast is at a play

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cinema buff goes to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a noun for a stage show but is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 Disney cartoon feature setting classical music to animation.

clue.text: The capital of Greece and the capital of Albania followed by the capital of Serbia

indicators.note: a capital is a word's opening letter as well as a seat of government, so only Albania's first letter is kept
again capital means the opening letter, so only Serbia's first letter is kept

blocks.note: then means after that, coming next

explanation.surface: A geography quiz listing three Balkan capitals in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'capital' is a real city; the other two mean capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the seat of the Greek government and the country's largest city.

clue.text: An embarrassing incident heard or observed

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the phrase sounds when spoken

blocks.note: making a scene is causing an embarrassing public fuss

explanation.surface: An awkward moment that people either overheard or witnessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen is the past participle of see, meaning noticed or watched, as observed is.

clue.text: Old artiste doing a turn in the grave?

definitions.note: a phrase describing a state, matched by the answer's participle phrase

indicators.note: turning things over moves them round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly performer doing one last act, or perhaps spinning in the grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing a turn' sounds like a variety performance by the artiste, but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone laid to rest has been buried, so they lie in their grave; the question mark marks the euphemism.

clue.text: Incendiary material can finish a tree

indicators.note: a word's finish is its final letter, so only the end of can is kept

blocks.note: a palm is a tropical tree

explanation.surface: A firebomb is able to destroy a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can finish' reads as 'is able to destroy'; it is the last letter of the word can.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied petrol mixture used in firebombs and flamethrowers, a fire-starting substance.

clue.text: Throw in a religious medal

indicators.note: 'in' places the word for throw inside the religious man

blocks.note: a religious is a member of a religious order, such as a friar

explanation.surface: Tossing a medal of saintly devotion into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' looks like an adjective for the medal, but here it is a noun: a monk or friar. The Africa Star was awarded for WWII service in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Africa Star is a British campaign decoration for Second World War service in North Africa, a military medal.

clue.text: Cigars with revolutionary origins

explanation.surface: Cigars whose roots lie in revolution, as Cuban cigars do.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheroots are cigars with both ends cut square, a particular type of smoking tobacco roll.

clue.text: Rattle's false alarm

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the given letters are a fake version needing rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone called Rattle raised a false alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False alarm' looks like one phrase, but 'false' is the signal and 'alarm' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden fright, which is what alarming them does.

clue.text: Petrol for van costing nothing

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective used as a noun for unleaded fuel

blocks.note: the van, or vanguard, is the lead position

explanation.surface: Filling up a van without paying for the fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' looks like a vehicle but means the front, the vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead-free fuel is unleaded motor spirit, sold without the tetraethyl lead additive once used.

clue.text: Notices about "Shine", say, or "Truly, Madly, Deeply", for example

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the notices go round the example word

blocks.note: shine is an example of a verb

explanation.surface: Posters for the films Shine and Truly, Madly, Deeply, both 1990s releases.
explanation.walkthrough: Shine and Truly, Madly, Deeply are both 1990s films, but here they are just words: a verb and three words of manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Truly, madly and deeply all modify verbs, describing how something is done, which makes them that part of speech.

clue.text: Bishop without polish

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop who has no polish, or lacks social refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like an instruction to remove letters, but it is simply the word lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Blacking is black shoe polish or boot blacking used to shine leather footwear.

clue.text: Moneylender receiving pence he takes unlawfully

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the lender holds the coin abbreviation inside

blocks.note: a usurer lends money at excessive interest
p is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: A loan shark pocketing pennies he has no right to.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper is someone who seizes a throne or power without legal right.

clue.text: Greek island importing clean dressed hides

indicators.note: a place importing goods takes them in, so the island surrounds the rest
dressed means arranged or prepared, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: Cos, or Kos, is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A Greek island imports cleaned, dressed animal skins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hides' reads as animal skins, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to keep it out of sight, exactly what hiding it means.

clue.text: Cats in the pound?

blocks.note: first meaning: the ounce is another name for the snow leopard
second meaning: units of weight, sixteen of which make one pound

explanation.surface: Stray cats kept in an animal pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound looks like the animal shelter but is the weight; the ounce is also an old name for the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: There are sixteen of these small weight units in an imperial pound, and the word is also a name for snow leopards.

clue.text: A woman in America or in another country

blocks.note: broad is American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman living either in the United States or elsewhere overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means overseas, living or travelling in a foreign land away from home.

clue.text: A prop on land

blocks.note: to shore up is to prop; a shore is a supporting beam

explanation.surface: A theatre or building prop set up on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on dry ground rather than at sea, the opposite of afloat.

clue.text: Odd sort of hand, etc

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A card player describes a strange hand, trailing off with etc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd sort of' reads as one phrase, but 'sort of' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc abbreviates et cetera, Latin for and the rest, used to cut a list short.

clue.text: Snow used as fuel

blocks.note: first meaning: snow is slang for cocaine
second meaning: the solid carbon residue of baked coal, burnt for heat

explanation.surface: Snow being shovelled onto a fire, oddly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is slang for cocaine, also called snow, and is also a smokeless fuel made from coal.

clue.text: Young reporter on a Caribbean island

blocks.note: a cub reporter is a novice journalist

explanation.surface: A trainee journalist assigned to a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean Sea, south of Florida.

clue.text: Poised, at ease, inwardly calm

indicators.note: inwardly points to letters inside the preceding words rather than their meaning

explanation.surface: Describing a composed person who is relaxed and serene within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poised' and 'at ease' look like synonyms for the definition; they hold the answer inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means quiet, unhurried and composed, close in sense to calm.

clue.text: Covering: for example, covering northern bird

indicators.note: something covering sits around the outside, so the example abbreviation wraps the rest

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
a robin is a small bird

explanation.surface: A list of things that cover, with an example of one covering a northern bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' appears twice: first as the definition, then as the instruction to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrobing means dressing or coating, as with a robe or a layer of chocolate, which is a covering.
